Background

The question translates integrality of a covering polyhedron into a compatibility condition between choices from a clutter and its blocker. A transversal meets each clutter edge, and blocker duality gives

b(b(C))=C; ideality is also preserved by taking the blocker. Thus the two selector maps are naturally paired. The proposed criterion is an application of polyhedral Sperner-type reasoning: for an ideal clutter, a suitable coloring of the facets of its covering polyhedron would force a vertex with all colors, which conflicts with the stipulated intersection condition. Pap (2012), §§1.4 and 3.3.8

The converse was conjectured by Tamás Király. Júlia Pap’s 2012 thesis presents it as a converse problem for the Sperner-based obstruction and establishes special cases. A central structural tool is Lehman’s theorem on minimally nonideal (mni) clutters: apart from the finite degenerate projective planes, an mni clutter and its blocker have cores whose minimum-size edges satisfy a highly regular incidence relation. Here a clutter is mni if it is nonideal but all its minors are ideal. Pap (2012), §§1.4 and 3.4.3 Egres Open, Orientation of nonideal clutters
